clue.text: Declare headquarters of previous occupant laudable and imposing

indicators.note: read as head quarters: the front quarter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the first two of its eight letters, a quarter
the first two of its eight letters, a quarter
the first two of its eight letters, a quarter
the first two of its eight letters, a quarter

explanation.surface: Someone praises the grand head office left behind by the last tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headquarters' looks like an office building, but it splits into head quarters: each of the four eight-letter words gives up its opening quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly, a straightforward synonym of declare.

clue.text: Secretaries visiting European capital begin to unwind together

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so the secretaries end up inside the capital

parts.note: the capital of France
PA, personal assistant, plural

indicators.note: the start of the following word is all that is wanted

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Assistants on a trip to Paris start to relax as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: Pari passu is Latin, used in English for things proceeding side by side on an equal footing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pari passu means at an equal pace or on equal terms, so simultaneously and side by side.

clue.text: Material from extreme characters attached to newspaper

parts.note: an organ is a publication speaking for a group
Z and A are the letters at the two ends of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Fabric made from the letters at the margins of a newspaper page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attached to' simply joins the two parts; the alphabet's ends come last here.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin stiff sheer fabric, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Looker's no good for soldier

indicators.note: having no good means the abbreviation for good is taken away

parts.note: someone who glances is a looker
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A handsome person proves unsuitable for military service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looker' wants to mean a handsome person; here it is literally one who looks, a glancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancer is a cavalry soldier armed with a lance.

clue.text: I'm deceptively relieving and persuasive

indicators.note: something done deceptively is disguised, so the letters appear in a misleading order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A smooth talker boasts of being soothing yet quietly convincing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the speaker's self-description: one who deceptively soothes and persuades.
explanation.definitionFit: An inveigler coaxes people by flattery or trickery, so the clue's charming, deceptive persuader describes one.

clue.text: Disreputable Nationalist spikes drink

indicators.note: spiking a thing means putting something into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: shady means of doubtful honesty
N is the abbreviation for Nationalist

explanation.surface: A dodgy nationalist slips something into someone's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spikes' looks like doping a drink, fitting the surface, but it just puts one letter inside a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a drink of beer mixed with lemonade.

clue.text: Hide a third of secondary notes

indicators.note: only one third of the following word, its opening three of nine letters, is wanted

parts.note: its first three letters
re is a note of the sol-fa scale
te is another sol-fa note

explanation.surface: Someone conceals part of their secondary-school notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' supplies two sol-fa syllables at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it, a synonym of hide.

clue.text: Fading legacy of setter that's gone west?

definitions.text: Fading legacy of setter that's gone west?

parts.words: Fading legacy of setter that's gone west?
parts.note: surface reading: what a crossword setter who has died leaves behind as their memory fades
setter's reading: the sun, which sets and goes down in the west, leaves a dimming light in the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' seems to be the compiler, and 'gone west' slang for dying; in fact the sun sets in the west.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterglow is the light remaining in the sky after sunset, which is what a setting sun leaves behind.

clue.text: Underwear for artists stored here?
Tiny portion of fish sent back

indicators.note: something sent back travels the other way, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A tiny portion of fish is returned to the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a scrap or shred of cloth, hence a tiny piece of something.

clue.text: The province of crazy avocations

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A region known for its residents' wild hobbies.
explanation.walkthrough: An avocation is a hobby or side occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nova Scotia is one of Canada's provinces, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: God discharged disease to rodents shortly affecting everyone

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

indicators.note: a word discharged is emptied of its contents, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: its first and last letters
mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: A deity unleashed a plague on rats and mice that spread universally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharged' sounds like releasing disease, but it empties the word down to its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A pandemic is a disease epidemic spread across a whole population, so widespread and touching all.

clue.text: Novice denied beginning money- making scheme

indicators.note: being denied a beginning means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a learner is a novice

explanation.surface: A beginner is refused start-up funding for a business plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is informal for something that generates income, such as a nice little earner.

clue.text: Clique controlling key committee membership?

indicators.note: something controlling another holds it in its grip, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a set is a social group
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: An inner circle decides the key positions on a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is a musical key, not an important one.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a seat on a committee means being a member of it, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Remove awful gushing from reworking of Wuthering Heights immediately

indicators.note: awful means dreadful or a mess, so the letters to be removed may come in any order
a reworking remakes something into a new form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
remove tells us to take some letters out of the longer phrase

parts.note: the novel's title, taken as written
taken as written, letters to be removed

explanation.surface: An editor cuts the overblown passages from an adaptation of Emily Brontë's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the letters of gushing out of Wuthering Heights leaves nine letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Therewith is an old-fashioned adverb meaning straight after that, i.e. at once.

clue.text: Tableware displayed in shop window?

parts.note: a plate is an item of tableware
a glass is another item of tableware

explanation.surface: A shop shows off its dinner service in the front window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tableware' supplies two items at once; the question mark flags that a shop window is an example of the material, not the material itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Plate glass is thick polished sheet glass, the kind used for large shopfronts, so it stands for a shop window.

clue.text: Couple bolstering score line in game

indicators.note: in a down clue, a support sits underneath, so this piece is written after the other

parts.note: a score is twenty
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A pair of players propping up their side's score in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, the twenty-two is the line twenty-two metres from each try line.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenty-two is a marked line on a rugby pitch, so a line in a game.

clue.text: The type to stir up passions without being given the lead?

indicators.note: the word given the lead goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: sans is French for without, also used in English

indicators.note: in a down clue, stirring up lifts a word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: fires are strong passions

explanation.surface: Asks what sort of person inflames emotions without being the ringleader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The type' sounds like a kind of person; it is a typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sans serif is a style of printing type without the small strokes at letter ends.

clue.text: Complete a French book by December 1st

parts.note: un is French for a
to book a table is to reserve it

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the month is taken

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Instruction to finish a French book before the start of December.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreserved support is complete, without any reservation or qualification.

clue.text: Where the young may be cultivated in Surrey (in one's absence)

definitions.text: Where the young may be cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated ground is turned over, so these letters are dug into a new order
in the absence of one, the letter standing for one is left out

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A place for raising seedlings or children somewhere in the county of Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south of London; 'cultivated' does double duty as part of the definition and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is where young plants are grown and also where young children are cared for.

clue.text: Greek component in methanol is perhaps used up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
in says the letters wanted sit inside the following words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Speculates that a Greek ingredient in methanol might be consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek component' is a part of the Greek alphabet, not a chemical ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, so one of its components.

clue.text: Displayed the choice of women's skirts

indicators.note: the outer letters wrap around the other piece, being its edges
a skirt is the outer edge, so only the outside letters are taken

parts.note: its first and last letters ignoring the apostrophe
or introduces a choice between alternatives

explanation.surface: Women show off the skirts they chose to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirts' looks like clothing, apt for worn, but it means the edges of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that is worn is on show, so worn can mean displayed on the body.

clue.text: Something to eat after play mounted in wood is finally done

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: oak is a hardwood

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means raised up, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: to act is to play a part

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A snack eaten once a play staged in the woods has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' just joins the letter from done onto the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An oatcake is a flat biscuit made of oatmeal, so something to eat.

clue.text: This could remove all signs of the times before our late queen

indicators.note: before says the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: eras are periods of time
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A wistful look at erasing all trace of the years before Elizabeth II's reign.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, used here of the late Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser is a rubber that rubs out pencil marks, so it can remove written signs.

clue.text: Barristers — potentially big cheeses holding forth from the outset?

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Bries are large soft cheeses, which can be big wheels

indicators.note: from the outset means only the word's opening letter is used

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Wonders whether lawyers are self-important bigwigs who hold forth at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big cheeses' sounds like important people, matching the barristers, but means actual cheeses. A brief is British slang for a barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal usage a brief is a barrister, the lawyer who takes on a case.

clue.text: Point covered by charges for computer system reruns

indicators.note: something covered by another thing sits underneath it, enclosed within it

parts.note: IT is information technology
E is a compass point, east
rates are charges or fees

explanation.surface: Talks about a computer system's charges, with one point hidden in the small print.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay backwards: charges for a computer system, IT RATES, cover a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat a process, so iterates means runs again.

clue.text: Cultivated elitist group oddly in a flap

explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flap' reads as agitated, but 'a flap' alone is the definition.

clue.text: Remove carbon monoxide choking North African city's atmosphere

indicators.note: remove says certain letters are taken out of the longer word

explanation.surface: A call to clear toxic fumes polluting the air of an Egyptian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choking' fits the pollution story and describes C and O sitting at either end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Air is the atmosphere around us; it also means the mood or feel of a place.

clue.text: What connects acid-heads and drug- pushers?

definitions.text: What connects acid-heads and drug- pushers?

parts.words: What connects acid-heads and drug- pushers?
parts.note: surface reading: what links LSD users with dealers, as if asking about a drugs network
setter's reading: the punctuation mark that joins the two halves of each compound word

explanation.walkthrough: The clue invites a story about the drug trade; the link is typographic, the little dash inside each phrase.

clue.text: Lousy ref somehow in good form

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters come in an unspecified order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor referee nevertheless manages to perform well.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer works in a sentence such as 'you seem yourself again', meaning well.
explanation.definitionFit: Being yourself means being in your normal healthy state, i.e. on good form.
